section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1969
title: 8 The variations in the incidence of accidental deaths in different regions result from a large number of factors peculiar to the region such as topography of the area, population, level of industrialisation and other socioeconomic factors. Considering population as one of the major concomitant variants, the volume of accidental deaths per one lakh of population in different States and Union Territories and cities has been estimated and is presented in Table 4. It shows that the highest number of accidental deaths occurred in the State of Maharashtra (22,825) followed by U.P. (17,796) M.P. (15,541) and West Bengal (13,135). All the Union Territories together accounted for only 2.5% of the total accidental deaths in the country. The highest volume of accidental deaths per one lakh of population was observed in Maharashtra (46.7) as against an average of 24.3, of all the States together. The volume of accidental deaths in Cities was consistently higher than the All-India average, the highest being recorded in Bombay (72.8) while the overall average for the Cities was (44.2). This pattern was noticed during 1968 also. TABLE 4
